questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral by Swapping the Order of Integration
questions.problem: Change the order of integration and evaluate the following double integral ${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{1}\frac{3{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{{x}^{6}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/a85f82756c621bf88b95451f54343be863345278f361fd0f0dd82f5d01c0cb5b.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{3}\le y\le 1}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary is

$$
y={x}^{3}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt[3]{y}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/8243a8c60e4b8b4846d330a00a090d6f93f94f17323c1d0a88d486ba77745451.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{1}\frac{3{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{{x}^{6}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{y}}\frac{3{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{{x}^{6}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{y}}\frac{3{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{{x}^{6}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{[\frac{2}{6}\sqrt{{x}^{6}+{y}^{2}}]}_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\sqrt{2{y}^{2}}-\sqrt{{y}^{2}})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y(\sqrt{2}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{(\sqrt{2}-1)}{2}[{y}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Partitioned Region
questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2x-2}^{1-{x}^{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/0119869a8627edfaf9c16f905908d378b94c9566b0a6b7742c813c35f58d4699.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,2x-2\le y\le 1-{x}^{3}}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/3fe0d83ae8f99f443646be4e84687104edaeef58a83e68da7e832630f31efda7.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$\,$ $x=\frac{y+2}{2}.$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{1-y}.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,0\le x\le \frac{y+2}{2}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{1-y}}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2x-2}^{1-{x}^{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{(y+2)/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{1-y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Partitioned Region
questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-y-2}^{0}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-2}^{0}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/9a539f69187276895f8f53e2107c1959fefd0aeb7126dcff049569bfc8bc49d3.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type II regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-y-2\le x\le 0}\,\cup \,{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y-2\le x\le 0}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=y-2\,⟹\,y=x+2,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
x=-y-2\,⟹\,y=-x-2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,-x-2\le y\le x+2},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/ba9c9132c8efdb811e63bebc05e1f46bc8cbc54bcb8246072013a75d53bcb4df.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-y-2}^{0}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-2}^{0}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-x-2}^{x+2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Partitioned Region
questions.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}-1}^{-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/926e4c717707d13fdb9562e149d2f41c3ab657b42fbae35c0953019ab93a06b6.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-{y}^{2}-1\le x\le -y}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/8933233e8aca4a36ee90ffec69ca6e93d0523d3fa50c400d2cdea78f9ec80812.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $y=y(x),$  are 

$\,$ $y=\sqrt{-x-1}\,$ and $\,y=1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=-x.$ 

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le -1,\,\sqrt{-x-1}\le y\le 1}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,0\le y\le -x}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{y}^{2}-1}^{-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{\sqrt{-x-1}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral by Swapping the Order of Integration
questions.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/8ed09966d887f66f36402df0047ba02444d92b8aa4c3cb744721bb4ad6278812.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,\sqrt[3]{y}\le x\le 0}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=\sqrt[3]{y}\,⟹\,y={x}^{3},
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=-1.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,-1\le y\le {x}^{3}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14079520/assets/f707a71f68f2e030696029d9a919e16ae6afda18a1d60dc3f8113f03143243e7.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{{x}^{3}}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)[{\int }_{-1}^{{x}^{3}}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)\cdot y\,{|}_{-1}^{{x}^{3}}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({x}^{3}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{4}+4x)\,{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡({0}^{4}+4(0))-(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡((-1)^{4}+4(-1))) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡3}{4} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡3-1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
